model.name: Plant Disease Detection Model V2 (MobileNetV2)
model.description: MobileNetV2 ONNX neural network for plant disease identification across 38 crop classes

low.description: Low severity - Early stage or cosmetic

classes.name: Apple Scab
symptoms: Olive-green to black velvety spots on leaves
Distorted or puckered foliage
Premature leaf drop
Scabby dark spots on fruit
classes.causes: Caused by fungus Venturia inaequalis, favored by cool, wet spring weather

treatment.chemical: Apply captan, myclobutanil, or copper fungicides starting at green tip stage
treatment.cultural: Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn to eliminate overwintering spores; prune trees for airflow
treatment.preventive: Plant scab-resistant apple cultivars like Honeycrisp, Liberty, or Enterprise

classes.urgency: Medium - treat during wet spring periods
classes.economic_impact: Can reduce fruit marketability and crop yield by 20-50%

classes.name: Apple Black Rot
symptoms: Frogeye leaf spots with purple borders and tan centers
Black rotting fruit with concentric rings
Cankers on branches and limbs
classes.causes: Fungus Botryosphaeria obtusa surviving in dead twigs and mummified fruit

treatment.chemical: Apply thiophanate-methyl or captan from petal fall through summer sprays
treatment.cultural: Prune out dead wood, fire blight strikes, and remove mummified apples
treatment.preventive: Avoid wounding bark during pruning or harvest; maintain tree vigor

classes.urgency: High - prune out infected branches immediately
classes.economic_impact: Can cause complete loss of fruit and branch dieback

classes.name: Cedar Apple Rust
symptoms: Bright orange-yellow circular spots on upper leaf surface
Small tube-like spore structures on leaf undersides
Premature defoliation
classes.causes: Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae fungus requiring junipers/cedars as alternate hosts

treatment.chemical: Apply myclobutanil or mancozeb at pink bud stage through petal fall
treatment.cultural: Remove nearby eastern red cedar or juniper trees within 1-2 miles if feasible
treatment.preventive: Choose rust-resistant cultivars (e.g., Freedom, Liberty, Redfree)

classes.urgency: Medium - apply fungicide before spring rains
classes.economic_impact: Defoliates trees and weakens fruit development

classes.name: Healthy Apple
symptoms: Vibrant green leaves without spots
Normal leaf margins and robust growth
Smooth clean fruit skin
classes.causes: No disease detected

treatment.chemical: No chemical treatment needed
treatment.cultural: Maintain balanced pruning, watering, and soil fertility
treatment.preventive: Continue routine orchard inspection and sanitation

classes.urgency: None - plant is healthy
classes.economic_impact: Optimal fruit quality and yield expected

classes.name: Healthy Blueberry
symptoms: Dark green, waxy leaves
Vigorous cane growth
No discoloration or wilting
classes.causes: No disease detected

treatment.chemical: None needed
treatment.cultural: Maintain acidic soil pH (4.5 - 5.5) and organic mulch
treatment.preventive: Ensure regular drip irrigation and weed control

classes.urgency: None - plant is healthy
classes.economic_impact: Healthy harvest expected

classes.name: Cherry Powdery Mildew
symptoms: White powdery fungal patches on leaves and young shoots
Curled or distorted young foliage
Stunted fruit growth
classes.causes: Fungus Podosphaera clandestina, favored by warm days, cool nights, and high humidity

treatment.chemical: Apply sulfur sprays, potassium bicarbonate, or myclobutanil
treatment.cultural: Prune canopy to promote sun penetration and air movement
treatment.preventive: Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization that stimulates overly tender growth

classes.urgency: Medium - spray upon first appearance of powdery patches
classes.economic_impact: Can distort foliage and reduce fruit sugar content

classes.name: Healthy Cherry
symptoms: Lush green foliage with serrated edges
Firm stems and healthy buds
No fungal coatings or spots
classes.causes: No disease detected

treatment.chemical: No treatment required
treatment.cultural: Standard pruning and irrigation practices
treatment.preventive: Regular orchard scouting for pests and fungal diseases

classes.urgency: None - plant is healthy
classes.economic_impact: High quality fruit yield

classes.name: Corn Gray Leaf Spot
symptoms: Rectangular, tan to gray lesions bounded by leaf veins
Lesions coalesce leading to blighting of entire leaves
Premature stalk lodging
classes.causes: Fungus Cercospora zeae-maydis surviving on surface crop residues

treatment.chemical: Apply strobilurin or triazole fungicides prior to silking if infection reaches upper canopy
treatment.cultural: Rotate with non-host crops (soybean) and incorporate crop residue
treatment.preventive: Select corn hybrids with high resistance ratings

classes.urgency: Medium - monitor infection pressure around tasseling
classes.economic_impact: Yield reduction between 15% and 40% under severe blighting

classes.name: Corn Common Rust
symptoms: Cinnamon-brown pustules on both upper and lower leaf surfaces
Powdery rust spores rubbing off on fingers
Leaf chlorosis around pustules
classes.causes: Fungus Puccinia sorghi, favored by moderate temperatures (16-25C) and high humidity

treatment.chemical: Fungicides such as azoxystrobin or pyraclostrobin if rust appears early on susceptible lines
treatment.cultural: Plant early in the season to avoid late-summer spore arrival
treatment.preventive: Use rust-resistant hybrid seed varieties

classes.urgency: Medium - treat if pustules appear before blister stage
classes.economic_impact: Yield loss up to 20% on sensitive sweet or field corn

classes.name: Corn Northern Leaf Blight
symptoms: Large cigar-shaped, grayish-green or tan lesions (2.5 to 15 cm long)
Dark fungal sporulation in damp conditions
Extensive premature death of leaves
classes.causes: Fungus Exserohilum turcicum, favored by cool, wet weather and heavy dews

treatment.chemical: Apply labeled fungicides (QoI or DMI group) if lesions appear before pollination
treatment.cultural: Rotate with soybean; till infected stubble under to accelerate breakdown
treatment.preventive: Plant hybrids with dominant Ht resistance genes

classes.urgency: High - protect ear leaf and upper canopy
classes.economic_impact: Can cause 30-50% grain yield loss if severe before silking

classes.name: Healthy Corn
symptoms: Deep green, uniform leaves
Sturdy stalks and full leaf canopy
No lesions or discoloration
classes.causes: No disease detected

treatment.chemical: None required
treatment.cultural: Maintain proper nitrogen fertility and soil moisture
treatment.preventive: Scout weekly during critical reproductive stages

classes.urgency: None - plant is healthy
classes.economic_impact: Maximum potential grain or ear yield

classes.name: Grape Black Rot
symptoms: Small reddish-brown circular spots on leaves with tiny black pycnidia
Berries turn brown, shrivel into hard black mummies
Cankers on shoots and tendrils
classes.causes: Guignardia bidwellii fungus, overwintering in mummified berries and canes

treatment.chemical: Apply mancozeb, captan, or myclobutanil starting at 1-3 inch shoot growth through post-bloom
treatment.cultural: Remove and destroy mummified clusters during dormant pruning; ensure canopy ventilation
treatment.preventive: Prune vines to open canopy and maximize sunlight and spray penetration

classes.urgency: High - critical spray window is from bloom to 4 weeks post-bloom
classes.economic_impact: Can destroy up to 80-100% of grape crop if untreated

classes.name: Grape Esca (Black Measles)
symptoms: Tiger-stripe leaf pattern: interveinal chlorosis and necrosis
Dark spots on fruit skins (measles)
Sudden apoplexy (wilting) of whole vine in summer heat
classes.causes: Complex of fungal vascular pathogens including Phaeomoniella chlamydospora and Fomitiporia

treatment.chemical: No effective curative chemical; seal pruning wounds with wound protectants
treatment.cultural: Avoid pruning in rainy weather; remove severely infected vines to protect vineyard
treatment.preventive: Use certified clean planting stock and sanitize pruning shears

classes.urgency: High - protect pruning cuts to prevent new infections
classes.economic_impact: Permanent vine decline and unmarketable fruit

classes.name: Grape Leaf Blight
symptoms: Irregular dark brown leaf spots with faint halos
Spots enlarge and merge causing leaf scorching
Premature defoliation late in season
classes.causes: Fungus Pseudocercospora cladosporioides (Isariopsis clavispora)

treatment.chemical: Copper-based fungicides or mancozeb applied during mid-to-late season
treatment.cultural: Prune out dense vegetation; clear fallen leaves post-harvest
treatment.preventive: Maintain proper vine spacing and canopy airflow

classes.urgency: Medium - treat if spreading before harvest
classes.economic_impact: Weakens vines and lowers winter hardiness

classes.name: Healthy Grape
symptoms: Broad green leaves with clean lobes and veins
Vigorous tendril and shoot extension
Clean berry clusters
classes.causes: No disease detected

treatment.chemical: None required
treatment.cultural: Continue balanced canopy management and shoot positioning
treatment.preventive: Routine vineyard monitoring

classes.urgency: None - plant is healthy
classes.economic_impact: Optimal fruit quality for table or winemaking

classes.name: Citrus Greening (HLB)
symptoms: Asymmetrical blotchy mottle on leaves
Yellowing of veins followed by leaf drop
Lopsided, bitter fruit that stays green at blossom end
Twig dieback
classes.causes: Bacterium Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus vectored by Asian citrus psyllid

treatment.chemical: Insecticide programs to manage Asian citrus psyllid vector populations
treatment.cultural: Remove and destroy confirmed infected trees immediately; provide foliar nutritional sprays
treatment.preventive: Use certified disease-free nursery stock in screened propagation houses

classes.urgency: Critical - report to local agricultural extension immediately
classes.economic_impact: Devastating disease causing tree death within a few years

classes.name: Peach Bacterial Spot
symptoms: Small angular dark purple spots on leaves that drop out (shot-hole effect)
Leaf yellowing and defoliation
Pitted dark lesions on fruit
classes.causes: Bacterium Xanthomonas arboricola pv. pruni, spread by blowing rain

treatment.chemical: Apply copper bactericides during dormancy and oxytetracycline during growing season
treatment.cultural: Avoid overhead watering; plant windbreaks in sandy soil regions
treatment.preventive: Choose resistant peach varieties (e.g., Redhaven, Biscoe, Reliance)

classes.urgency: Medium - protect foliage and fruit from petal fall to cover sprays
classes.economic_impact: Severe fruit blemishes and yield reduction

classes.name: Healthy Peach
symptoms: Long, lanceolate bright green leaves
Clean bark and strong new shoot growth
Blemish-free foliage
classes.causes: No disease detected

treatment.chemical: None required
treatment.cultural: Maintain annual open-center pruning and orchard irrigation
treatment.preventive: Scout regularly for peach leaf curl and borers

classes.urgency: None - plant is healthy
classes.economic_impact: Full peach yield expected

classes.name: Bell Pepper Bacterial Spot
symptoms: Water-soaked leaf lesions turning brown with yellow halos
Leaves curl and drop prematurely
Raised, blister-like rough spots on peppers
classes.causes: Xanthomonas campestris pv. vesicatoria spread through splashing rain and handling

treatment.chemical: Apply copper hydroxide mixed with mancozeb sprays at 7-10 day intervals
treatment.cultural: Avoid working in wet fields; remove diseased plant debris at season end
treatment.preventive: Plant certified pathogen-free, resistant seed hybrids (Race 1-5 resistance)

classes.urgency: Medium - spray promptly during warm rainy weather
classes.economic_impact: Can cause extensive defoliation and sunscald on exposed fruit

classes.name: Healthy Bell Pepper
symptoms: Glossy dark green leaves without holes or spots
Erect bushy growth habit
Clean blossoms and sturdy fruit set
classes.causes: No disease detected

treatment.chemical: None required
treatment.cultural: Consistent watering to prevent blossom end rot; balanced fertilization
treatment.preventive: Regular pest scouting for aphids and thrips

classes.urgency: None - plant is healthy
classes.economic_impact: High marketable pepper yields

classes.name: Potato Early Blight
symptoms: Dark brown target-like concentric ring spots on older leaves
Chlorosis surrounding leaf spots
Premature yellowing and leaf loss
classes.causes: Fungus Alternaria solani, favored by alternating wet and dry periods

treatment.chemical: Apply chlorothalonil, mancozeb, or azoxystrobin at initial symptom observation
treatment.cultural: Ensure adequate nitrogen and potassium fertility; rotate crops with non-solanaceous crops
treatment.preventive: Irrigate in morning so foliage dries quickly before nightfall

classes.urgency: Medium - treat before disease advances up the canopy
classes.economic_impact: Can reduce tuber size and total harvest weight by 20-30%

classes.name: Potato Late Blight
symptoms: Water-soaked dark lesions spreading rapidly across leaves
White fuzzy mold on underside of leaves in humid conditions
Brown rotten tubers with foul odor
classes.causes: Oomycete Phytophthora infestans (the pathogen of the Irish Potato Famine)

treatment.chemical: Apply protectant fungicides (mancozeb, chlorothalonil) or systemic options (metalaxyl, mandipropamid)
treatment.cultural: Destroy volunteer potato plants and cull piles; kill vines before harvest to protect tubers
treatment.preventive: Plant certified disease-free seed potatoes; space rows for air circulation

classes.urgency: High - treat immediately upon detection; can destroy field in days
classes.economic_impact: Can cause complete crop collapse in cool, humid weather

classes.name: Healthy Potato
symptoms: Vibrant green compound leaves
Dense upright foliage canopy
No blight spots or wilting
classes.causes: No disease detected

treatment.chemical: None required
treatment.cultural: Hill soil around stems; maintain steady soil moisture
treatment.preventive: Weekly scouting for Colorado potato beetle and blight symptoms

classes.urgency: None - plant is healthy
classes.economic_impact: Full potential tuber production

classes.name: Healthy Raspberry
symptoms: Healthy palmate leaves with silvery undersides
Vigorous cane development
Clean stems without cankers
classes.causes: No disease detected

treatment.chemical: None required
treatment.cultural: Prune spent canes annually; trellis canes for air movement
treatment.preventive: Keep planting beds mulched and weed-free

classes.urgency: None - plant is healthy
classes.economic_impact: Sweet, plentiful berry harvest

classes.name: Healthy Soybean
symptoms: Trifoliate rich green leaves
Clean sturdy stems and vigorous pod development
Uniform healthy stand
classes.causes: No disease detected

treatment.chemical: None required
treatment.cultural: Standard field weed management and soil fertility
treatment.preventive: Routine field scouting through reproductive stages

classes.urgency: None - plant is healthy
classes.economic_impact: Maximum soybean yield potential

classes.name: Squash Powdery Mildew
symptoms: White talcum-powder-like spots on upper and lower leaf surfaces
Leaves turn yellow, brown, and become brittle
Premature vine defoliation causing sunburnt fruit
classes.causes: Fungus Podosphaera xanthii, thriving in warm, dry weather with high humidity

treatment.chemical: Apply potassium bicarbonate, neem oil, sulfur, or trifloxystrobin
treatment.cultural: Remove and compost infected leaves; avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizer
treatment.preventive: Plant powdery-mildew-resistant squash varieties; space plants widely

classes.urgency: Medium - spray when first white patches appear on older leaves
classes.economic_impact: Reduces fruit sweetness, size, and storability

classes.name: Strawberry Leaf Scorch
symptoms: Numerous small, irregular purplish spots on upper leaf surfaces
Spots enlarge and merge, turning foliage brown and scorched
Calyx and fruit stems may also show purple lesions
classes.causes: Fungus Diplocarpon earlianum, spread by splashing water

treatment.chemical: Apply captan or thiophanate-methyl during early spring leaf emergence and post-bloom
treatment.cultural: Renovate strawberry beds after harvest; mow and dispose of old infected leaves
treatment.preventive: Plant in well-drained soil with full sunlight; use drip irrigation

classes.urgency: Medium - treat during wet spring periods
classes.economic_impact: Weakens plants and lowers fruit size and yield

classes.name: Healthy Strawberry
symptoms: Lush trifoliate green leaves with serrated edges
Healthy crown and vigorous runner production
Clean, glossy green leaves
classes.causes: No disease detected

treatment.chemical: None required
treatment.cultural: Maintain straw mulch under berries; avoid water stress during fruiting
treatment.preventive: Inspect crowns and leaves regularly

classes.urgency: None - plant is healthy
classes.economic_impact: High berry production and berry quality

classes.name: Tomato Bacterial Spot
symptoms: Small, dark, water-soaked spots on leaves that turn brown/black
Leaves look ragged with yellow halos around spots
Black raised scabs on green tomatoes
classes.causes: Bacterium Xanthomonas spp., spread by splashing rain and warm humid weather

treatment.chemical: Apply copper fungicides combined with mancozeb, or use Actigard / Bacillus subtilis
treatment.cultural: Do not work around wet tomato plants; stake and prune plants for air circulation
treatment.preventive: Use certified pathogen-free seed; practice a 2-3 year crop rotation

classes.urgency: Medium - spray at first sign of spotting during wet weather
classes.economic_impact: Defoliates plants, causes sunscald and unmarketable fruit

classes.name: Tomato Early Blight
symptoms: Concentric target-like rings on lower leaves
Yellowing around spots spreading to entire leaf
Stem lesions near soil line and sunken dark fruit rot
classes.causes: Fungus Alternaria solani, overwintering on plant debris and solanaceous weeds

treatment.chemical: Apply copper sprays, chlorothalonil, or azoxystrobin every 7-10 days
treatment.cultural: Mulch around base to prevent soil splash; prune lower 12 inches of leaves as plant grows
treatment.preventive: Water only at base using drip irrigation; remove diseased debris in autumn

classes.urgency: Medium - treat promptly before spreading to upper canopy
classes.economic_impact: Can cause 20-40% yield loss if left unchecked

classes.name: Tomato Late Blight
symptoms: Large pale-green to brown water-soaked lesions on leaves
White fuzzy growth under leaves in humid mornings
Stems develop brown greasy lesions; fruit rots rapidly
classes.causes: Oomycete Phytophthora infestans, thriving in cool, humid, rainy weather

treatment.chemical: Apply preventative chlorothalonil or copper sprays, or cymoxanil/metalaxyl when active
treatment.cultural: Remove and bag infected plants immediately; do not compost late-blight-infected material
treatment.preventive: Choose late-blight-resistant cultivars (e.g., Defiant, Mountain Magic, Iron Lady)

classes.urgency: High - immediate action required to save the crop
classes.economic_impact: Can destroy entire tomato plantings within a single week

classes.name: Tomato Leaf Mold
symptoms: Pale green or yellowish spots on upper leaf surfaces
Olive-green to velvety brown mold growth on underside of leaves
Leaves wither and drop prematurely
classes.causes: Fungus Passalora fulva (Cladosporium fulvum), common in high humidity greenhouse/tunnel environments

treatment.chemical: Apply copper-based fungicides, chlorothalonil, or biofungicides (Bacillus amyloliquefaciens)
treatment.cultural: Reduce relative humidity below 85% with ventilation and fans; prune suckers
treatment.preventive: Water at root zone in morning; choose leaf-mold-resistant tomato hybrids

classes.urgency: Medium - improve greenhouse airflow immediately
classes.economic_impact: Premature defoliation reduces fruit size and quantity

classes.name: Tomato Septoria Leaf Spot
symptoms: Numerous small circular spots (1.5-3mm) with dark brown margins and gray/white centers
Tiny black specks (pycnidia) visible inside spots
Severe lower-leaf yellowing and leaf loss
classes.causes: Fungus Septoria lycopersici, spread by water splashes from soil onto lower leaves

treatment.chemical: Apply copper fungicides, chlorothalonil, or mancozeb at 7-14 day intervals
treatment.cultural: Mulch beneath plants immediately after transplanting; remove bottom leaves showing spots
treatment.preventive: Avoid overhead watering; rotate away from tomatoes, potatoes, and eggplants for 2+ years

classes.urgency: Medium - remove infected bottom leaves and spray protectant
classes.economic_impact: Causes progressive upward defoliation and exposes fruit to sunscald

classes.name: Tomato Spider Mites
symptoms: Fine pale stippling or yellow speckling on upper leaf surfaces
Fine webbing on leaf undersides and stem junctions
Leaves turn bronze, dry out, and drop
classes.causes: Tetranychus urticae mites, thriving in hot, dry, dusty environmental conditions

treatment.chemical: Apply insecticidal soap, neem oil, horticultural oils, or abamectin (ensure full coverage under leaves)
treatment.cultural: Hose down plants with a strong stream of water to knock off mites and disrupt webbing; keep soil adequately moist
treatment.preventive: Encourage or release predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis); avoid broad-spectrum pesticides that kill natural predators

classes.urgency: Medium - treat before mite populations explode in heat
classes.economic_impact: Stunts plant growth and impairs photosynthesis

classes.name: Tomato Target Spot
symptoms: Brown circular lesions with concentric target rings and light-brown centers
Lesions appear on both foliage and green fruit
Fruit spots are sunken with dark centers
classes.causes: Fungus Corynespora cassiicola, favored by warm, humid tropical and subtropical weather

treatment.chemical: Apply azoxystrobin, chlorothalonil, or boscalid following label guidelines
treatment.cultural: Improve row spacing and prune lower leaves to promote rapid drying of canopy
treatment.preventive: Use disease-free transplants and eliminate solanaceous weeds around fields

classes.urgency: Medium - treat early in flowering and fruit development
classes.economic_impact: Causes foliage loss and direct fruit rotting

classes.name: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus
symptoms: Severe upward curling and cupping of leaflets
Interveinal yellowing (chlorosis) of margins
Severe plant stunting with bushy appearance and flower drop
classes.causes: Begomovirus transmitted exclusively by the sweetpotato whitefly (Bemisia tabaci)

treatment.chemical: Control whitefly vectors using systemic insecticides (e.g., imidacloprid) or insecticidal soaps
treatment.cultural: Eradicate and bag infected plants immediately to prevent whitefly transmission to neighbors
treatment.preventive: Use reflective silver mulches to repel whiteflies; plant TYLCV-resistant hybrids (e.g., Tycoon, Sanibel)

classes.urgency: High - remove infected plants and manage whitefly vector
classes.economic_impact: Can cause up to 100% loss of fruit set if infection occurs early

classes.name: Tomato Mosaic Virus
symptoms: Mottled light and dark green mosaic patterns on leaves
Distorted, narrow, or fern-like leaf growth
Internal browning of fruit walls and uneven ripening
classes.causes: Tobamovirus transmitted mechanically via contaminated tools, hands, tobacco products, and seeds

treatment.chemical: No chemical cure exists for viral plant infections
treatment.cultural: Wash hands and tools with milk or 10% trisodium phosphate (TSP); rogue out infected plants
treatment.preventive: Plant resistant varieties (indicated by T or ToMV on seed packets); avoid smoking near plants

classes.urgency: High - rogue out infected plants immediately and disinfect equipment
classes.economic_impact: Permanently stunts plants and makes fruit unmarketable

classes.name: Healthy Tomato
symptoms: Deep green, vibrant compound foliage
Vigorous indeterminate or determinate growth
Clean flowers, strong stems, and smooth fruit
classes.causes: No disease detected

treatment.chemical: None required
treatment.cultural: Prune suckers, support vines with cages or stakes, and maintain consistent watering
treatment.preventive: Scout foliage weekly and mulch soil to protect lower leaves

classes.urgency: None - plant is healthy
classes.economic_impact: Optimal tomato harvest yield and fruit quality
